Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:1.hebrew: גולפי - מקום קבוצת אנשים ונשים, או לדרשה או לחופה, היה מסדר קנקנים של חרס הרבה ביניהם, שאם יבאו זה אצל זה — יקשקשו וישמע קול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:1.english: Pitchers - [In] a gathering place of men and women, either for a sermon or for a wedding canopy, he would arrange many earthenware pitchers between them, so that if they were to come toward one another, [the pitchers] would rattle and a sound would be heard.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:2.hebrew: דייר - לשון דרי דרי (מגילה דף יב.) — שורות שורות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:2.english: Would arrange rows - An expression of "dari dari" (Megillah 12a) — rows upon rows.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:3.hebrew: דייר קנה - מסדר קנים, שהעובר עליהן קולם נשמע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:3.english: Arranged reeds - [He would] arrange reeds, so that when someone passes over them, their sound is heard.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:4.hebrew: סקבא דשתא ריגלא - ריעוע של ימות השנה ליחוד ולעבירה — ימות הרגל, שיש קבוצת אנשים ונשים לשמוע דרשה, ונותנים ונושאים זה עם זה. סקבא — דדרישדור"א בלע"ז, כמו "דמסקב להו לחמרייהו" (ב"מ דף כז:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:10:4.english: The wound of the year is the Festival - The vulnerable time among the days of the year for [forbidden] seclusion and for sin is the days of the Festival, as there is a gathering of men and women to hear the sermon, and they interact with one another. *Sakva* — *redoissedure* in Old French [a sore or flaw], like “that causes sores on their donkeys” (Bava Metzia 27b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:1.hebrew: שקולו דרגא - שאכלו בעליה, וירדו רב יוסף ואשתו, והוא נשאר בעליה. שקולו דרגא מתותי ביבי, שלא ירד ויתיחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:1.english: They removed the ladder - For they ate in the upper chamber, and Rav Yosef and his wife went down, while he [Bibi] remained in the upper chamber. They removed the ladder from beneath Bibi, so that he would not come down and be alone [with them].

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:2.hebrew: אסוקינהו - שצוה עליהם לפדותם, ונתנום בעלייתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:2.english: They brought them up - For he commanded concerning them to redeem them, and they placed them in his upper chamber.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:3.hebrew: בהדי דקא חלפא חדא מינייהו - שהיתה עוברת אצל פי ארובה שמן העלייה לבית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:3.english: As one of them was passing - For she was passing by the opening of the skylight [that leads] from the upper chamber to the house.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:4.hebrew: נפל נהורא באיפומא - נפל אור בבית דרך פי העליה, מפני שהיו פניה מאירות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:4.english: A light fell in the aperture - Light fell into the house through the opening of the upper chamber, because her face was shining.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:11:5.english: And he was climbing - To demand her for himself.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:12:1.english: He parted [his legs] - He spread and parted his legs to stand firmly in his place, [in order] to overcome his evil inclination.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:12:2.hebrew: אמר נורא בי עמרם - הזעיק בני השכונה ליאסף ולבא לכבות הדליקה, כדי שיחדל מיצרו, שיתבייש מהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:12:2.english: He said: "Fire in the house of Amram" - He summoned the residents of the neighborhood to gather and come extinguish the fire, so that he would desist from his [evil] inclination, as he would be ashamed before them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:12:3.english: The Sages came - For they thought that there was a fire there.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:12:4.english: He adjured him - Rav Amram [adjured] the evil inclination to depart from him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:1.hebrew: מתלוצץ בעבירה - אומר שנקל הוא להתגבר על יצרו, אם היו רוצים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:1.english: Would ridicule sin - Saying that it is easy to overcome one's [evil] inclination, if they wanted to.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:2.english: Satan appeared to him - Who is the evil inclination:

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:3.english: On the other side of the ferry - To the other side, which is across the water:

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:4.english: There was no ferry - Ferry boats.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:5.hebrew: נקט מצרא - חבל מתוח משפת הנהר אל שפתו, ואוחזין בו לבא על דף קצר המוטל ברוחב הנהר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:5.english: He took hold of a rope - A rope stretched from [one] bank of the river to its [other] bank, and [people] hold onto it to walk across a narrow plank laid across the width of the river.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:13:6.english: He left him - The evil inclination [left] Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:14:1.english: And he was climbing - In order to solicit her [for sin].

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:15:1.english: At the table - They eat at the table.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:15:2.hebrew: וכיבי - ולנ"ץ (מלנ"ץ: פצע), המוציאין ליחה ומאוסין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:15:2.english: And sores - Volanz (malanz: wound), which exude pus and are repulsive.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:1:1.hebrew: לאתרויי ביה - שאם יבא עליה, אין מים בודקין אותה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:1:1.english: To warn him - That if he engages in intercourse with her, the [bitter] waters will not test her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:2:1.english: They taught only - That which [the Mishnah] says: 'A woman may seclude herself with two men.'

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:2:2.english: Lest one [of them] need to relieve himself - And he will need to distance himself out of modesty.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:2:3.hebrew: דניהוו עליה סהדי - אם יבא עליה, ויעידו לפני ב"ד, ולא ימחו עליה מגילה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:2:3.english: That they should be witnesses against him - If he engages in intercourse with her, and they will testify before the court, so that they will not erase the scroll [of the sotah] for her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:3:1.english: Raise your feet - Hurry to walk, so that we get ahead of her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:3:2.english: Such as us - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:3:3.hebrew: רבי חנינא בר פפי וחביריו - רבי צדוק ורב כהנא בפ"ק (לעיל קידושין דף מ.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:3:3.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi and his colleagues - [Namely,] Rabbi Tzadok and Rav Kahana, [mentioned] in the first chapter (above, Kiddushin 40a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:4:1.english: One is flogged for seclusion - [Lashes for] rebelliousness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:4:2.english: And they do not forbid - A married woman to her husband on account of seclusion.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:4:3.english: They did not say - That [the court] flogs.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:4:4.hebrew: אתה מוציא לעז - שיאמרו: ראוה שזינתה, לכך הלקוה — והאידנא ליכא מיתת בית דין למיקטלינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:4:4.english: You cast an aspersion - For [people] will say: "They saw that she committed adultery, [and] that is why they flogged her" — and nowadays there is no capital punishment by the court to execute them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:5:1.hebrew: מר זוטרא מלקי - על ייחוד אשת איש, ומכריז עליה שלא זינתה, אלא נתיחדה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:5:1.english: Mar Zutra would flog - For seclusion with a married woman, and he would proclaim concerning her that she did not commit adultery, but rather had secluded herself.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:6:1.hebrew: על לא טובה השמועה - מי שיוצא קול עליו שהוא עובר עבירות, מלקין אותו. דלא טובה השמועה — לאו הוא, דכתיב בבני עלי: ״אל בני״ — לאו יש כאן על ״לא טובה השמועה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:6:1.english: Due to a bad report - One about whom a rumor spreads that he is committing transgressions, they flog him. For “a bad report” is a negative commandment, as it is written concerning the sons of Eli: “No, my sons” — there is a negative commandment here regarding a bad report.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:6:2.hebrew: אפסרה - קבשטר"א (קיבישטר"א: אפסר (חלק מהרתמה, שבו מושכים את הבהמה או את הסוס בצווארם)):
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:6:2.english: A halter - Chevestre [in Old French, a halter] (kivestre: a halter [part of the harness by which an animal or a horse is led by its neck]).

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:6:3.hebrew: ומקרי ליה - קורא לפניו "אל בני", להודיע שעל לאו זה הוא לוקה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:6:3.english: And recite before him - He reads before him: “No, my sons,” to make known that he is being flogged for this prohibition.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:7:1.hebrew: בעלה בעיר אין חוששין לה משום יחוד - להלקות, דמסתפי מבעל — השתא אתי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:7:1.english: [If] her husband is in town, there is no concern on her account regarding seclusion - To administer lashes, as [the man] is afraid of the husband, [thinking,] “Now he will come.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:7:2.hebrew: שקולו דרגא - שאכלו בעליה, וירדו רב יוסף ואשתו, והוא נשאר בעליה. שקולו דרגא מתותי ביבי — שלא ירד ויתיחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:7:2.english: Remove the ladder - For they had eaten in the upper story, and Rav Yosef and his wife went down, and he remained in the upper story. [He said,] “Remove the ladder from beneath Beivai” — so that he would not go down and be secluded [with her].

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:7:3.english: His friend - An ally to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:8:1.english: Men on the outside - In the outer room.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:8:2.hebrew: ונשים בפנימי אין חוששין משום יחוד - שהחיצונים אין להם דרך לפנים, ואיך יתייחד האיש אחד עם הנשים? אבל הפנימים יש להם דרך לחוץ. הילכך, אנשים בפנים ונשים בחוץ — חוששין שמא יצא אחד מהם ויתייחד עם הנשים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:8:2.english: And women in the inner [room], there is no concern due to seclusion - For those in the outer [room] have no pathway to the interior, and how could an individual man be secluded with the women? But those in the inner [room] have a pathway to the outside. Therefore, [if there are] men on the inside and women on the outside, there is concern lest one of them go out and be secluded with the women.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:9:1.hebrew: איפכא - אנשים בחוץ ונשים בפנים — חוששין, שמא יכנס האחד לפנים ולא ירגישו בו חביריו. אנשים בפנים ונשים בחוץ — אין חוששין שמא תכנס היא לפנים; ואם תכנס היא לפנים — לא איכפת לן, דאשה מתייחדת עם שני אנשים. ואם אחד מהן יוצא לבין הנשים — אין זה ייחוד, דמיסתפי שמא יצא אחד מהן אחריו, שהרי דרך הפנימיים על החיצונים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81a:9:1.english: The opposite - [If] men are outside and women are inside, we are concerned lest one [of them] enter inside and his companions will not notice him. [If] men are inside and women are outside, we are not concerned lest she enter inside; and [even] if she enters inside, we do not care, as a woman may be secluded with two men. And if one of them goes out among the women, this is not [forbidden] seclusion, for he is afraid lest one of them go out after him, for the path of those in the inner [room] is through [the quarters of] those in the outer [room].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 81a:10:1.hebrew: סקבא דשתא ריגלא - פירוש: ריעוע של ימות השנה לייחוד ולעבירה — כלומר: ימות הרגל, [שיש] קבוצות אנשים ונשים לשמוע הדרשה, ונותנין עין זה על זה. וי"א: לכך נהגו להתענות לאחר פסח ולאחר סוכות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 81a:10:1.english: "The vulnerable point of the year is the Festival" - Explanation: [It is] a vulnerable time among the days of the year for [forbidden] seclusion and sin — that is, the days of the Festival, [when there are] gatherings of men and women to hear the sermon, and they cast their eyes upon one another. And some say: For this reason, [people] were accustomed to fast after Pesach and after Sukkot.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 81a:4:1.hebrew: מלקין על הייחוד - פי' בקונטרס דמיירי בפנויה, דהכי מוקי לה בסמוך, ו"אין אוסרים על הייחוד" מיירי בייחוד אשת איש. וקשה: דאם כן, לצדדין קתני — רישא בפנויה וסיפא באשת איש?! ונראה לפרש, דסיפא נמי מיירי בפנויה, ולאוסרה לכהן משום זונה. ומיהו קשה: דתנן בפ"ק דכתובות (דף יג.): "היתה מעוברת, ואמרו לה: מה טיבו של עובר זה? מאיש פלוני, וכהן הוא — רבי יהושע אומר: אינה נאמנת", ופריך עליה בגמרא מהא דאמר רב הכא: "אין אוסרין על הייחוד", ומשני: "מעלה עשו ביוחסין". ולפי מה שפירשתי דמיירי לאוסרה לכהן, לא משני גמרא התם מידי, דהא הכא מיירי ליוחסין, ואפ"ה אמרינן דאין אוסרין! ויש לומר: דלעולם מיירי ליוחסין, והא דמשני התם "מעלה עשו ביוחסין" — שאני התם דאינה נאמנת משום דמודה היא שנבעלה; והכא דקאמר דאין אוסרין, היינו משום דאינה מודה שנבעלה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 81a:4:1.english: They flog due to seclusion - The Kuntres explained that [this clause] deals with an unmarried woman, as [the Gemara] establishes nearby, and "they do not forbid due to seclusion" deals with the seclusion of a married woman. And this is difficult: For if so, [Rav] is teaching [his statement] disjunctively — the first clause regarding an unmarried woman, and the latter clause regarding a married woman?! And it seems [preferable] to explain that the latter clause also deals with an unmarried woman, and [means] to forbid her to a priest on account of [suspected status as] a zonah. However, this is difficult: As we learned in a Mishnah in the first chapter of Ketubot (13a): "If she was pregnant, and they said to her: 'What is the nature of this fetus?' [and she replied:] '[It is] from so-and-so, and he is a priest' — Rabbi Yehoshua says: She is not believed," and the Gemara objects against him from that which Rav said here: "They do not forbid due to seclusion," and [the Gemara] answers: "They applied a higher standard regarding lineage." And according to what I explained, that [Rav's statement here] deals with forbidding her to a priest, the Gemara there has not answered anything! For here too it deals with lineage, and even so we say that they do not forbid [her]! And one can say that indeed it deals with lineage; and that which [the Gemara] answers there, "They applied a higher standard regarding lineage" — there it is different, in that she is not believed because she admits that she had intercourse; whereas here, where [Rav] says that they do not forbid [her], that is because she does not admit that she had intercourse.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 81a:7:1.hebrew: בעלה בעיר אין חוששין לה משום יחוד - פי' בקונטרס: אין חוששין להלקות. משמע מתוך פירושו: הא איסורא מיהא איכא. וקשה: דאם כן, מאי פריך בסמוך על רב יוסף דקאמר "שקולו דרגא מתותי ביבי": "והאמר רבה: בעלה בעיר אין חוששין לה משום יחוד"? ומאי קושיא? נהי דמלקות ליכא, איסורא מיהא איכא! ונראה לפרש: אין חוששין כלל משום יחוד, ואפילו איסורא ליכא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 81a:7:1.english: "Her husband is in town, there is no concern for her due to seclusion" - The Kuntres explained: "There is no concern" to administer lashes. It is implied from his explanation that there is nonetheless a prohibition. And this is difficult: For if so, why does [the Gemara] challenge Rav Yosef just below, who said, "Remove the ladder from beneath Beivai": "But didn't Rabba say: '[If] her husband is in town, there is no concern for her due to seclusion'"? And what is the difficulty? Granted that there are no lashes, there is nonetheless a prohibition! And it appears [correct] to explain: There is no concern at all due to seclusion, and there is not even a prohibition.
